articles.title: Katy Perry faces opposition from more than 360 neighbours over proposed 110-acre California youth camp; residents raise wildfire, traffic and noise concerns as singer’s foundation defends Gratitude Canyon project
articles.summary: Pop superstar Katy Perry is facing growing opposition from residents in California’s Goleta Valley over plans to build a permanent youth camp and arts
articles.body: Pop superstar Katy Perry is facing growing opposition from residents in California’s Goleta Valley over plans to build a permanent youth camp and arts centre on a 110-acre property. More than 360 neighbours have signed a petition opposing the proposed development, citing concerns about wildfire safety, traffic, noise and the possibility of the site hosting events outside the summer camp season.The project, called Gratitude Canyon, is being developed by Perry and her sister, Angela Lerche, through their nonprofit organisation, the Firework Foundation. Located at 183 Winchester Canyon Road, the proposed facility is intended to provide arts, music and nature-based programmes for underserved children.However, residents living in nearby neighbourhoods believe the development could significantly change the character of their community. While some have said they support Perry's efforts to help young people, they argue that the proposed location is unsuitable for a facility of this scale.According to a report by local news outlet Noozhawk, more than 360 residents had signed an online petition against the proposal as of November 1, 2026.What does Katy Perry’s Gratitude Canyon project include?The proposed Gratitude Canyon development would provide a permanent home for Camp Firework, the youth sleepaway programme run by Perry's foundation. The camp is intended to serve middle-school-aged children through activities focused on creativity, self-expression, arts and outdoor exploration.Plans for the 110-acre property include eight cabins, accommodation for counsellors, a dining hall, a gymnasium, a swimming pool, tennis and pickleball courts, an amphitheatre and a recording studio. The development would also include outdoor recreation areas and other facilities for campers.According to the project website, only around 3% of the property would be occupied by built structures, with the remaining land retained as open landscape, orchards, habitat areas and outdoor spaces.The foundation's broader aim is to expand the work of Camp Firework by creating a permanent facility in the Santa Barbara County region. The organisation has already hosted multiple youth camps, offering children from underserved communities opportunities to explore music, dance, hiking and other creative activities.Why are residents opposing Katy Perry’s proposed youth camp?Residents from nearby communities, including Winchester Commons and other neighbourhoods around Winchester Canyon, have raised objections to the proposed development.One of their main concerns is the possibility that the project could bring increased traffic and activity to an otherwise quiet residential area. Neighbours argue that a permanent facility with multiple amenities and the potential for off-season events could have a much wider impact than a conventional summer camp.Sandra McGreevy, one of the residents who spoke to Noozhawk, clarified that the opposition was not directed at Perry's charitable work.“We have zero problem with (Katy giving back to the community),” she told the publication.Residents have also questioned why the application includes provisions for special events outside the regular camp season. Deborah Holmes said she did not object to the idea of a nature camp but wanted greater clarity about the additional events and how they would be monitored.The project's proposed activities have become a central point of disagreement, with residents seeking assurances that the facility would operate primarily as a youth camp rather than become a venue for larger gatherings.Wildfire evacuation and traffic safety become major concernsFire safety is another significant issue raised by residents. Neighbours have pointed out that the area has limited road access, with one main street serving the surrounding community.They fear that a wildfire could create dangerous evacuation conditions if residents, campers, staff and visitors all needed to leave the area at the same time.The petitioners have also questioned whether the project's fire safety assessment adequately accounts for the number of people who could be present during special events and other peak-attendance periods.According to Noozhawk, residents believe the evacuation arrangements need closer scrutiny before the project can move forward.The Gratitude Canyon team, meanwhile, says fire safety and vegetation management have been considered as part of the planning process. The project has involved consultation with the Santa Barbara County Fire Department, as well as Robert Lewin, a former Santa Barbara County emergency management director and former San Luis Obispo fire chief.The foundation's team has also said that fire protection measures and emergency planning are important components of the proposal.Residents worry about noise and off-season eventsApart from fire safety, neighbours are concerned about the possibility of noise travelling across the canyon and disturbing nearby homes.Residents have described the surrounding landscape as a naturally enclosed area where sound can carry over considerable distances. Jen Lilienstein, who organised the online petition, told Noozhawk that the canyon's natural shape could amplify noise from activities at the proposed camp.“The canyon is a naturally occurring bowl,” she said, explaining that even sounds from the surrounding environment can be heard in the neighbourhood.Lilienstein added that residents were concerned about the long-term impact on their quality of life.“We are middle-class people who can’t afford to just pick up and move somewhere else because this happens,” she said.The foundation's project team has disputed the suggestion that the camp would create excessive noise. According to Noozhawk, acoustic modelling submitted by the project team indicated that sound levels at the nearest property boundary would remain below the county benchmark. The camp would also have quiet hours.Another point of concern is the proposal to allow up to four special events a year, each with a maximum attendance of 400 people. Residents have questioned how parking, traffic and noise would be managed during these gatherings.The project team has said the events would be limited and subject to management measures. It has also maintained that the facility is not intended to operate as a commercial concert or wedding venue.What has Katy Perry’s foundation said in response?The Firework Foundation has defended Gratitude Canyon as a project designed to benefit young people while preserving much of the property's natural character.On its project website, the foundation describes the proposed facility as a place offering underserved children opportunities in the arts, nature exploration and creative expression.The organisation says that the development would occupy only a small portion of the 110-acre site, leaving approximately 97% of the property as open landscape.The foundation has also argued that the proposal offers an alternative to more intensive forms of development that could otherwise be considered for the land.The project has received support from local youth organisations, including Girls Inc. of Greater Santa Barbara and the United Boys & Girls Club Santa Barbara. Both organisations have been associated with the foundation's youth initiatives.In June 2026, the proposal was reviewed by the Santa Barbara County South Board of Architectural Review. Board members supported the revised architectural plans, although the meeting was not a final approval of the overall development.Board member Valerie Frosch praised the design, describing the proposed buildings as beautiful. Another board member, Jerry Rocci, said he believed the project could have a relatively low impact on the surrounding community.However, the board also raised questions about aspects such as the entrance design and traffic flow, while making clear that the project still had several stages to complete before it could receive approval.When will Katy Perry’s youth camp get approval?Gratitude Canyon remains in the early stages of the county's review process. Santa Barbara County planners have requested additional information from the project team, and the environmental impact report process has not yet begun, according to Noozhawk's November 1 report.An environmental scoping hearing is expected early next year. The proposal will also have to undergo the required review under the California Environmental Quality Act, which examines potential environmental effects and opportunities to address them.Because the project involves proposed changes to land-use rules, it will require further consideration by county officials. Public hearings before the County Planning Commission and, subsequently, the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors are part of the approval process.For now, the proposed Gratitude Canyon development remains a point of contention between the Firework Foundation and neighbouring homeowners. While Perry and her sister see it as an opportunity to create a lasting resource for underserved children, residents want stronger assurances about its impact on their homes, safety and surroundings.The debate is likely to continue as the project moves through the county's planning and environmental review process.You use AI every day. articles.title: A fuel-card company promised small businesses savings but charged them hundreds of millions in hidden fees; it has now agreed to pay $100 million
articles.summary: A fuel-card provider that marketed its services as a way for small businesses to cut petrol costs has agreed to pay $100 million to resolve allegations
articles.body: A fuel-card provider that marketed its services as a way for small businesses to cut petrol costs has agreed to pay $100 million to resolve allegations that it charged customers hundreds of millions of dollars in undisclosed fees. FleetCor Technologies, now known as Corpay, and its chief executive Ronald Clarke reached a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission after courts found the company had violated consumer protection law. The agreement is intended to provide financial relief to affected businesses following years of litigation over charges customers allegedly did not know they were paying.How FleetCor’s fuel cards allegedly cost small businesses moreAccording to the Federal Trade Commission, FleetCor promoted its fuel cards as a means of helping businesses save money on petrol while managing expenses and controlling spending. However, the agency alleged that the company’s customers, overwhelmingly small businesses, were charged a range of fees that had not been properly disclosed or authorised.The FTC said the charges amounted to hundreds of millions of dollars and affected tens of thousands of customers. The alleged practices included undisclosed fees, charges customers had not agreed to pay and late fees imposed even when businesses had paid on time or had been prevented from making payments on time.The dispute centred on the difference between the savings businesses expected from fuel cards and the costs they allegedly incurred through additional charges. For companies operating vehicles and managing regular fuel purchases, such fees could undermine the financial benefits the cards were supposed to provide.The FTC also alleged that FleetCor misrepresented the savings available through its fuel cards, along with their fraud-control features and associated fees.Why were the charges difficult for customers to noticeThe FTC’s complaint described a billing system that allegedly made additional fees difficult to identify. FleetCor often began charging certain fees only after several billing cycles had passed, according to the agency. This delay meant customers could initially use the cards without seeing the full range of costs.The problem was compounded by the way bills were presented. The FTC alleged that FleetCor’s invoices did not clearly show that fees were being charged, leaving customers to consult separate account-management reports to find them. Even there, some charges were buried among other information or were missing altogether.For businesses trying to keep track of fuel spending, this arrangement allegedly made it harder to understand what they were being charged and whether the cards were delivering the promised savings.The allegations were not limited to poor disclosure. The agency maintained that some charges were unauthorised, meaning customers had neither been properly informed about them nor agreed to pay them.How did the dispute reach the settlementThe FTC first filed its federal court complaint against FleetCor and Clarke in 2019. The case challenged the company’s fee practices and its representations about the benefits of its fuel cards.A major development came in 2023, when a federal district court granted summary judgment to the FTC on all counts. According to the regulator, the court found that FleetCor had imposed hidden or otherwise unauthorised fees and misrepresented the savings and charges associated with its cards.The court also imposed a permanent order restricting the company’s conduct. FleetCor was prohibited from billing customers for charges without their informed consent and clear, unavoidable information about those charges. The order also barred the company from concealing important fee information behind hyperlinks and from making deceptive claims about its fuel cards.The litigation continued beyond that ruling. In 2026, a federal appeals court upheld the judgment against FleetCor on all counts and affirmed the permanent injunction. It also upheld the judgment against Clarke on all but one count, while vacating the injunction as it applied to him.These court decisions established the legal backdrop for the subsequent agreement with the FTC.What does the $100 million agreement coverThe September 2026 settlement provides for FleetCor and Clarke to pay $100 million to resolve the FTC’s administrative action. The agency said the money would be used to compensate business customers harmed by the company’s alleged practices.The settlement is significant because it follows the court findings rather than simply ending an investigation into allegations. The FTC had already secured relief through the federal court proceedings, and the administrative agreement adds a further financial remedy for affected customers.According to the FTC, FleetCor and Clarke have also agreed not to oppose the reimposition of a federal court injunction against Clarke. This provision follows the appeals court decision that upheld most of the judgment against him but vacated the injunction previously imposed in his case.The agreement was accepted by the FTC through a consent process, with the commission recording a 1-0-1 vote. Chairman Andrew N Ferguson was recused from the decision.What restrictions will apply to FleetCorIt requires the company to obtain express and informed consent before billing for charges, while making information about those charges clear and unavoidable.It also prevents FleetCor from hiding important details about fees behind hyperlinks. This is intended to ensure that customers can understand the costs associated with their accounts without having to search through separate documents or navigate away from the information presented to them.The order further prohibits deceptive claims about the company’s fuel cards. That restriction addresses the FTC’s allegations that FleetCor overstated the savings businesses could achieve and misrepresented features linked to fraud protection and fees.The FTC noted that violations of a final consent order could carry civil penalties of up to $53,088 for each violation.The settlement is designed to return money to customers who suffered losses from FleetCor’s practices. However, the FTC’s announcement did not specify individual payment amounts or provide a detailed timetable for distributing the funds.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Iran speaker: Ball in Trump administration court to prevent renewed war
articles.summary: Iran’s chief negotiator says it’s on the United States to stop a return to all-out war after Tehran gave Washington a “firm and rational response” to its demands around nuclear weapons and opening the Strait of Hormuz. Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf did not specify what “response” he was referring to, though the comments came after the…
articles.body:
Iran’s chief negotiator says it’s on the United States to stop a return to all-out war after Tehran gave Washington a “firm and rational response” to its demands around nuclear weapons and opening the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf did not specify what “response” he was referring to, though the comments came after the U.S. on Monday conducted what it said were defensive strikes on an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Qeshm Island and Hengam Island, both in the Strait of Hormuz.

President Trump on Tuesday confirmed the attack, which took place a day before the U.S. midterm elections, describing it as “minor” rather than a return to full conflict.

Speaking to Fox News by phone Tuesday, Trump said Washington watched as Iran spent roughly two months building the facility, which reportedly included radar detectors and missile launchers.

“We watched it get built, as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely,” he said.

Current diplomacy between the U.S. and Iran is shaky at best as both sides have been engaged in indirect talk s via Qatari mediators. Vice President Vance reportedly reached out to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei in recent days as part of efforts to restart talks.

Trump has given mixed messages as to what he plans to do next, for weeks threatening to authorize major combat operations against Tehran after the midterms while also pushing for a peace deal.

Vance on Monday said that he and Trump “both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement.”

The U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, which began Feb. 28 and led to Tehran’s closure of the vital Strait of Hormuz, has led to soaring fuel costs across the globe — an issue that has crippled the Republican Party ahead of elections.

Iran has made any concessions on the strait or its nuclear program contingent on the U.S. lifting its naval blockade on Iranian ports, waiving sanctions on Iranian oil sales, and demanding a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon, among other stipulations.

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them,” Rezaei wrote on social media Tuesday. “Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

articles.title: Voter poll: What have US voters named the top issues at the midterms?
articles.summary: A major election day survey suggests voters are the most unhappy with the economy.
articles.body:
The economy and the state of democracy have been named as the top issues for US voters, according to an election day poll.

The survey - officially called the Voter Poll - asks tens of thousands of the American electorate their opinions and motivations, and providing a breakdown by age, gender, education and other demographics.

Polling company SSRS collects data on behalf of a consortium of news companies, and the survey is a representative sample of American voters in the run up to the election, and includes exit polling of both early and on the day voters.

Here are some of the breakdowns from the 2026 voter poll. Like all surveys they are estimates; the numbers are also likely to be updated as more data arrives.

Some 39% of those asked in the poll of more than 79,000 people said the economy was the most important issue, while 32% put the state of democracy top.

Following that, immigration was named most important by 14% of voters while healthcare, foreign policy and crime were ranked first by a lower share.

Data suggests the majority of US voters have a negative view of the state of the national economy.

Some 75% of those asked said the economy was in a "not so good or poor" state with 25% saying it was "excellent or good".

Looking at their own family finances, 44% of people said they were in a worse situation than two years ago, 38% said about the same and 18% said better.

Majority say Trump's policies 'worsened economy'

Almost two thirds (65%) of voters surveyed say US President Donald Trump's policies have worsened economic conditions in the US.

By contrast, 28% say Trump's policies have improved conditions and only 8% say the president has had no impact.

People were also asked whether expressing support or opposition for Trump was one reason for their midterm vote.

Some 43% said expressing opposition was a reason but a similar proportion (41%) said he was not a factor. Only 16% of those asked said expressing support was a reason for their vote.

Almost four in ten of those asked (38%) said they were angry at the way things are going in the US at the moment, with a further 37% saying they were dissatisfied.

Only 18% said they were satisfied, and 7% of respondents felt enthusiastic.

So taken together, there is a majority telling pollsters SSRS they are not happy about the current state of the country.

Separately, a large majority, 90%, also said that government corruption was a crucial or major factor in their vote.

Inflation has caused hardship for most Americans

As well as broader issues, pollsters also asked about inflation and the impact of rising prices on people's lives.

Almost eight in 10 voters (79%) said inflation had caused them and their family a severe or moderate hardship in the past year. A fifth (21%) of those answering said it had caused them no hardship at all.

A majority of voters (59%) said they were "very concerned" about the cost of petrol and diesel and a similar proportion (58%) gave this answer about the cost of food and groceries.

More than six in 10 respondents (62%) said they thought that higher than usual prices were more because of Trump's policies.

And 38% said it was more due to factors beyond his control.

Majority say US 'made wrong decision on Iran'

The voter poll also said that around six in 10 (62%) of those asked said the US made the wrong decision to take military action against Iran. Four in 10 (38%) said it was right.

Separately, three-quarters of voters (74%) said the conflict was a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress and a quarter (26%) said it was a minor factor or not a factor.

Voting patterns differ by age and gender

The voter poll gives an insight into how different groups of voters have cast their ballots.

Nationally, the data suggests women have backed Democratic candidates for the House by 57%, to 41% for Republicans. Men appear to be divided with just under half voting for each party.

By age, almost two-thirds of people aged under 45 said they voted Democrat. The middle-aged group, 45-64, are split with 49% backing the Democrats and 48% voting Republican.

Slightly more than half of those aged over-65 said they voted Republican and 47% for Democratic candidates.

White voters have voted for Republican candidates by 51% to 47% for Democrats, according to estimates.

All other groups have voted more for Democratic candidates, with Hispanic and Latino voters breaking for them by an estimated 60% compared to 35% for Republicans.

Voters without a college education voted more for Republicans in this election, by 51% to 45% Democrat, the survey suggested.

People with a college degree have voted Democrat by an estimated 61% to 36% Republican.

All these numbers are for the national picture, voting patterns will vary state by state.

articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até 31 de dezembro; sorteio será realizado em 1º de janeiro de 2027. No ano passado, seis apostas dividiram prêmio recorde de R$ 1,09 bilhão.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até 31 de dezembro; sorteio será realizado em 1º de janeiro de 2027. No ano passado, seis apostas dividiram prêmio recorde de R$ 1,09 bilhão.
articles.body:
Imagens de lotérica e cartões de apostas da Mega Sena da Virada, loteria com prêmio previsto de R$ 600 milhões. Caxias do Sul, RS (27). 27/12/2024 - Foto: — Foto: Antonio Machado/FOTOARENA/Estadão Conteúdo

O sorteio da Mega da Virada 2026 será realizado às 11h do dia 1º de janeiro de 2027, com prêmio estimado em mais de R$ 1 bilhão.

No ano passado, a Caixa também adiou o concurso especial para 1º de janeiro, às 10h, alegando a necessidade de ajustes operacionais.

As apostas começaram nesta terça-feira (3) e poderão ser feitas até as 22h do dia 31 de dezembro de 2026.

Em 2025, a Mega da Virada pagou o prêmio recorde de R$ 1,09 bilhão, superando a estimativa inicial de R$ 850 milhões. Seis apostas acertaram as dezenas sorteadas, e cada uma recebeu mais de R$ 181,8 milhões.

As regras da Mega da Virada são as mesmas dos concursos regulares da Mega-Sena. Para conquistar o prêmio principal, é necessário acertar os seis números sorteados, entre os 60 disponíveis. Também há premiações para quem acertar cinco (quina) ou quatro números (quadra).

A principal diferença é que o prêmio da Mega da Virada não acumula. Caso ninguém acerte as seis dezenas, o valor destinado à faixa principal é distribuído entre os acertadores da quina. Se também não houver ganhadores nessa faixa, o prêmio passa para os acertadores da quadra.

Para jogar, os apostadores podem ir a uma das mais de 13 mil lotéricas da caixa espalhadas pelo Brasil. Além disso, as apostas podem ser feitas pela internet, de forma prática e segura.

A seguir, veja o passo a passo para apostar pela internet:

Acesse o site da Loterias Caixa e faça login.

Se ainda não tiver cadastro, será preciso criar uma conta com seus dados pessoais.

Após entrar, escolha a opção Mega da Virada.

Preencha o volante virtual escolhendo os números da aposta.

Se preferir, o sistema pode escolher os números automaticamente (Surpresinha) ou você pode comprar cotas de bolão.

Depois de escolher a aposta, clique no Carrinho, no canto superior direito da página, para conferir os jogos.

Para finalizar, faça o pagamento com cartão de crédito ou Pix.

Baixe o aplicativo Loterias Caixa na Play Store (Android) ou App Store (iOS).

Se for o primeiro acesso, será necessário se cadastrar com seus dados pessoais.

Selecione os números da aposta ou use a opção Surpresinha, em que o sistema escolhe os números para você.

Vá até o carrinho de apostas, localizado na parte inferior da tela.

Finalize o pagamento com cartão de crédito ou Pix..

A aposta mínima, de 6 números, custa R$ 6,00. Quanto mais números marcar, maior o preço da aposta.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: King calls slavery 'monstrous' and 'Celeb loses gag bid'
articles.summary: The King's comments on the transatlantic slave trade and the high-profile celebrity who lost a "gag bid" in sex claim case lead Wednesday's papers.
articles.body:
King Charles III's speech describing slavery as "monstrous" makes the front of the i Paper , but the paper points out that he stopped short of offering an apology to Commonwealth leaders. The Daily Mail calls the address "punchier-than-expected" with the monarch insisting "we cannot change the past". "Pointedly", the Mail says, the King "reminded them that the Royal Navy led the way in ending the transatlantic slave trade".

The Daily Telegraph leads on its campaign to scrap what's described as a "chilling" trans law. It suggests the legislation risks criminalising parents who question whether their children are trans. Writing in the Telegraph , a former chair of the Equality and Human Rights Commission, Baroness Falkner, describes the law as an "unprecedented and unwarranted intrusion into family life". The government says the draft bill will "outlaw a specific form of abuse", while setting high bars that protect regular parenting.

Silhouettes of a still unnamed male celebrity feature on a number of front pages after he failed in a bid at the High Court to have his identity protected in relation to allegations of sexual misconduct. "Sex Pest Loses Gag Bid", is the Sun's headline , with a pen scribbled over where the name would be. The paper says the star is accused of inappropriate and exploitative sexual activities with multiple young women. The Daily Star reports that the celeb's identity will stay "secret for now", pending any appeal.

The Financial Times says that the Conservatives have turned to the former Prime Minister Lord Cameron, "to charm donors" and build on Kemi Badenoch's revival. He is described as the "star attraction" for a Cities of London and Westminster Conservative association event next month where tickets will cost up to £345 a seat. "He's a big draw", is the view of one ex-Tory MP.

And finally, Kellogg's has announced that Rice Krispies will no longer be made with rice grains. The new formulation will instead be a mix of rice flour and corn flour. The change has left the Times to ask: "presumably they will continue to be crispy".

images.caption: The i Paper leads with King Charles III's comments on slavery during his address at the Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda. "King says slavery was 'monstrous'," reads the paper's headline, although he "stops short of apologising". Instead, it writes the King praised the "Royal Navy's role in ending the transatlantic slave trade" at the meeting.

articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe, no explosive devices found
articles.summary: At least seven flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship received threats, but officials say searches found no explosives.
articles.body:
A series of bomb threats against passenger flights across Europe has prompted emergency searches, briefly shut down an airport outside the Polish capital, Warsaw, and led the Italian Air Force to escort a Ryanair plane into Rome.

All of the threats on Tuesday turned out to be false.

At least seven flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship were targeted, according to officials. All of the planes landed safely, and searches found no explosives.

The airlines affected included Ryanair, Wizz Air, Scandinavian Airlines and the Polish carrier LOT. Ryanair, the Irish budget carrier, appeared to be the hardest hit, with four of its flights to different destinations being targeted.

No one claimed responsibility, and officials did not attribute blame.

The incidents came a day after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary after receiving a similar bomb threat while in the air.

In Poland, two Warsaw-bound flights were targeted.

Scandinavian Airlines Flight SK751 from Copenhagen landed without incident at Warsaw Chopin Airport, which closed a runway while the plane was inspected.

“The passengers disembarked, the plane landed normally; it was not an emergency landing,” Alexandra Lindgren Kaoukji, a spokesperson for the airline, told the Polish news agency PAP. She said the matter has been referred to the Polish police.

A LOT Polish Airlines flight from London’s Heathrow, which was also due at Chopin, was diverted to the city’s second airport, Warsaw Modlin, which was closed after the alert.

The plane, a Boeing 737 Max, landed safely. “Nothing was found,” said Adam Szablowski, a spokesman for Modlin. Airport officials said normal operations later resumed.

In Italy, two Eurofighter jets escorted Ryanair Flight FR9611 from Dublin into Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, where it landed at 10:45am local time, the airport’s operator said.

The Italian Air Force said it had responded immediately to “a report of a suspected threat aboard a civilian aircraft”.

An earlier Ryanair flight from Lisbon that landed at Fiumicino at 9:40am was also subjected to anti-bomb procedures. Checks of passengers, luggage and the plane “were all negative and the alert was lifted,” the operator said.

In Spain, Aena, the national airport operator, said it had activated an emergency protocol “due to a bomb alert” on a Ryanair flight from Manchester.

The plane landed in Murcia at 10:30am without incident.

In Bulgaria, a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo, Italy, was inspected after landing in the country’s capital, Sofia, a spokesperson for the Bulgarian Interior Ministry said. A Ryanair flight from Dublin to Sofia was also targeted, the country’s transport ministry said. No explosives were found on either plane.

The threats followed a similar episode on Monday, exwhen a Wizz Air flight from London’s Luton Airport to Sofia received a bomb threat in midair and was diverted to Budapest.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on Facebook that NATO’s air-defence alert service had flagged the flight. He said Hungarian Gripen fighter jets “took to the air within minutes” and escorted it safely to the ground.

In the United Kingdom, London’s Metropolitan Police said it had been made “aware of threats against … four aircraft due to depart from or arrive at Heathrow Airport”, one of Europe’s busiest hubs, on Tuesday.

It also received a further warning involving a flight at Manchester Airport.

After checks, police said “no security issues were identified,” without giving further details.

Late on Tuesday, the Greek Coast Guard said a Panama-flagged cruise ship, the Crown Iris, had been evacuated while anchored off the island of Syros after a bomb threat.

The ship was carrying about 1,500 passengers and crew and was bound for Haifa, Israel. No device was found, and the ship was expected to resume its voyage.

While no country pointed fingers over the bomb threats, they came at a time when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as “hybrid attacks” and acts of sabotage.

Moscow and Tehran both deny any such campaign.

This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of low-cost, deniable disruption efforts.

Rhys Jones, analysis output manager at aviation risk advisory firm Osprey Flight Solutions, said that seven confirmed bomb threats in a single day affecting flights was exceptional.

“The lack of clear target state, airline or route indicates that general disruption to aviation operations is the aim,” Jones told Reuters.

articles.title: Google to everyone saying 'company threatened schools over using AI; says: We want to clarify, we are giving more …
articles.summary: A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year.
articles.body: A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year. Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, told The New York Times that the company’s AI features are “deeply integrated” into Search, meaning students cannot access one without the other. Soon after the announcement, many politicians and leaders including Bernie Sanders and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani voiced their outrage on social media. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Zohran Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter). Bernie Sanders wrote that “Google is threatening schools,” referring to the policy as “extortion.”The company has now responded to the claims issuing the clarification on the change. “We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less,” Google wrote on X.In the post, Google clarified that while Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF by default, Schools will be in control. They can choose to turn ON one, two, or all of these services individually, the tech giant said.Here’s what Google saidWe want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced:- Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default. This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control over student use of AI services.- Schools are in control: They can choose to turn ON 🟢 one, two, or all of these services individually.- We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control. That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.Schools should have control over AI in classroom: GoogleThe company also published a blog post where it said that “schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach”.“After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on,” it said.“We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition. Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.We’ll continue to listen to feedback and evolve our approach as we work in partnership with schools, teachers, pedagogical experts, and parents on helping the next generation learn and thrive”.You use AI every day. articles.title: Abraham Teklu Lemma: US contractor gave Ethiopia secrets to help kill Tigray fighters
articles.summary: The Ethiopian-born American citizen admitted sharing dozens of classified documents with senior Ethiopian officials.
articles.body:
An Ethiopian-born American citizen has pleaded guilty to passing highly classified intelligence to Ethiopia, including information he hoped would help target and kill fighters during the country's 2020 civil war.

Abraham Teklu Lemma, a former US contractor, admitted sharing dozens of classified documents and photographs with senior Ethiopian officials over more than two years, the US Department of Justice said.

"In doing so, he betrayed his oath, his colleagues, and his country, while jeopardizing our national security," said US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

The 54-year-old faces up to 22 years in prison under a plea agreement, with sentencing scheduled for next April.

Abraham had worked as a contractor at the State Department, Justice Department and National Reconnaissance Office, the agency responsible for US intelligence satellites.

Prosecutors said Abraham worked with senior figures in Ethiopia's political, military and intelligence establishments between 2021 and his arrest in August 2023.

He secretly removed classified material from secure government facilities, sometimes copying sensitive information into handwritten notes that he carried out of the buildings. He used his position as an IT administrator to extract electronic intelligence files.

"Much of the highly classified information Lemma shared with the Ethiopian government concerned an armed conflict in Ethiopia," prosecutors said.

The information included satellite imagery and details of military activities, which he passed to Ethiopian officials through encrypted messages.

The FBI said Ethiopian officials subsequently used intelligence supplied by Abraham in military operations.

Prosecutors said he hoped the information would help Ethiopia's military identify and kill paramilitary fighters.

"Lemma betrayed the United States to an extraordinary degree," said John Eisenberg, the US assistant attorney general for national security.

In one message to an Ethiopian official in December 2021, he wrote: "We have to finish these people once and for all, otherwise there will never be peace in Ethiopia," court papers showed.

Later that day, he shared further intelligence and urged the official: "Please send Dro[nes]."

How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

The revelations shed light on how sensitive American intelligence was passed to Ethiopian authorities during a devastating civil war that killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

He was arrested in Maryland in August 2023 following an investigation into his handling of classified intelligence.

At the time, prosecutors alleged that had removed security markings from intelligence reports and shared information with a foreign intelligence official.

In one exchange, the official asked him to continue providing assistance, to which Lemma replied: "Roger that!"

Pirro, the US attorney, said Abraham had abused his access to some of America's most sensitive intelligence.

She accused him of betraying his colleagues and country with prosecutors saying he "will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law".

Abraham pleaded guilty to conspiring to transmit national defence information to a foreign government.

His sentencing is scheduled for 14 April 2027.

The two-year conflict, which began in November 2020, pitted Ethiopian federal forces and their allies against fighters from the northern Tigray region.

It was marked by widespread allegations of atrocities, including massacres, sexual violence and attacks on civilians.

A peace agreement signed in November 2022 ended the main fighting, although tensions and insecurity have persisted.

articles.title: Former elementary school teacher becomes newest paper billionaire in China
articles.summary: A former elementary school teacher has been propelled into the ranks of paper billionaires in China after the stock debut of his company selling tape and other adhesive products to tech giants, according to Forbes.
articles.body: A former elementary school teacher has been propelled into the ranks of paper billionaires in China after the stock debut of his company selling tape and other adhesive products to tech giants, according to Forbes. Michael Mai, chairman and CEO of Crown New Materials Technology, entered the rarefied financial heights on Tuesday when the company, which produces binding agents for major brands like Tesla and Apple, made its trading debut on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Shares shot up as much as 787%, from 16.98 yuan ($2.55) per share in its stock filing to a height of 150.58 yuan ($22.57) per share at one point, according to the Shenzhen bourse, mainland China’s second-largest stock exchange. Mai, an Australian citizen and permanent resident of Hong Kong, has an estimated net worth of $2.5 billion, based on his stake in the firm, Forbes reported. The 62-year-old was reportedly an elementary school teacher in the southern Chinese city of Zhongshan – where the company, founded in 2000, is based. His sister, Mai Huixia, 64, who serves as vice-chairperson, joined him in the billionaire ranks, with Forbes reporting that her stake gave her a $2 billion fortune. Shares eased to about 77 yuan ($12) per share Wednesday morning following the peak a day earlier that prompted the company to call on investors in a statement to “invest rationally.” CNN has reached out to the company for comment. With four manufacturing plants across China and one in Vietnam, the company specializes in products that bind components found in a range of retail products, from vehicle roofs to semiconductors in smartphone, according to its website. China’s stock markets have taken a hit in recent months amid weak consumer spending and concerns over a possible bursting of the AI bubble. Since peaking in June, key Chinese indexes have fallen more than 20%, crossing the threshold for a bear market. Beijing responded two weeks ago by pumping $19 billion into exchange-traded funds, according to Bloomberg data, its biggest intervention since early 2025, when US President Donald Trump’s tariff offensive roiled global markets.
